details.title: Master Professional Services Agreement
details.courts_or_seat: state or federal courts located in Harris County, Texas

governing_law_source.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Texas, without regard to its conflict of laws principles... Any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be brought exclusively in the state or federal courts located in Harris County, Texas, and each Party irrevocably submits to the personal jurisdiction of such courts.

details.parties_quote: This Master Professional Services Agreement (together with all Exhibits, Statements of Work and amendments hereto, this "Agreement") is entered into as of the date of the last signature below (the "Effective Date") by and between Harrington Health Systems, Inc., a Texas nonprofit corporation with its principal place of business at 6400 Fannin Street, Suite 1800, Houston, Texas 77030 ("Harrington" or "Client"), and AtliQ Inc, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 101 College Road East, Suite 210, Princeton, New Jersey 08540 ("Contractor").

payment_source.quote: Client shall pay each properly submitted, undisputed invoice within ninety (90) days after Client's receipt thereof.

details.services_summary: Design and implement an enterprise clinical and operational analytics platform, dashboards, readmission-risk predictive model, and knowledge transfer.

liability_cap.basis: Client's aggregate liability is capped at fees actually paid. Contractor's liability is unlimited (nothing in the agreement limits or excludes Contractor's liability for any losses).
liability_cap.quote: CLIENT'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES ACTUALLY PAID BY CLIENT TO CONTRACTOR UNDER THIS AGREEMENT. NOTHING IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL LIMIT OR EXCLUDE CONTRACTOR'S LIABILITY FOR ANY LOSSES, WHETHER DIRECT OR INDIRECT, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, INCLUDING CONTRACTOR'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, BREACH OF THE BAA, OR ANY DATA SECURITY INCIDENT.

delay_penalty.quote: Accordingly, if Contractor fails to achieve any Delivery Date, Contractor shall pay Client, as liquidated damages, an amount equal to two percent (2%) of the Total Contract Value for each calendar day from the Delivery Date until the date the applicable Deliverable is accepted.

details.one_sided_note: Article 6 defines Confidential Information generally, but Section 6.5 specifically grants injunctive relief to Client for breaches by Contractor without mentioning reciprocal remedies for Contractor.
details.mentions_baa_or_dpa: "Business Associate Agreement" or "BAA" means the business associate agreement attached hereto as Exhibit D.

insurance_requirements.quote: commercial general liability of $2,000,000 per occurrence
professional liability/errors and omissions of $5,000,000 per claim

restrictive_covenants.summary: All deliverables are works made for hire and assigned to Client.
restrictive_covenants.restricted_activity: Assigning intellectual property rights in deliverables and pre-existing materials
restrictive_covenants.quote: All Deliverables shall be deemed "works made for hire" as defined in the U.S. Copyright Act, 17 U.S.C. § 101, and shall be the sole and exclusive property of Client from creation... Contractor hereby irrevocably assigns, transfers and conveys to Client all right, title and interest therein

restrictive_covenants.summary: No PHI shall be accessed, stored, or processed outside the United States without prior written consent.
restrictive_covenants.restricted_activity: Accessing, storing, or processing PHI outside the US
restrictive_covenants.quote: No PHI shall be accessed, stored or processed outside the United States without Client's prior written consent. Any Contractor Personnel located outside the United States shall access only de-identified data within Client-controlled environments.

findings.title: Delay penalty with no cap and no exclusion for client-caused delay
findings.why: AtliQ could pay for delays it did not cause (Brightwater).
findings.comparison: Past contracts cap penalties at 5% of the milestone and exclude client delay (3 of 3).
findings.quote: Accordingly, if Contractor fails to achieve any Delivery Date, Contractor shall pay Client, as liquidated damages, an amount equal to two percent (2%) of the Total Contract Value for each calendar day from the Delivery Date until the date the applicable Deliverable is accepted.

findings.title: Cyber insurance of $5,000,000 required; AtliQ holds $1M
findings.why: AtliQ would be in breach on signing.

findings.title: Unlimited Rejection and Refund Right
findings.why: Allows indefinite testing and full fee refunds, exposing AtliQ to severe revenue clawback.
findings.comparison: Standard is to fix or re-perform, not provide unconditional refunds of all fees paid.
findings.quote: Client may repeat the acceptance process until the Deliverable conforms, or may, at its option, reject the Deliverable and receive a refund of all Fees paid in respect thereof.

findings.title: Broad Cross-Agreement Set-off
findings.why: Allows client to withhold payments due under this contract for disputes under unrelated agreements.
findings.comparison: Exposes AtliQ to unilateral withholding across multiple projects.
findings.quote: Client may set off against any amount owed to Contractor any amount owed by Contractor to Client under this Agreement or any other agreement.

findings.title: Unpaid work in progress on termination for convenience
findings.why: AtliQ is not paid for work in progress or uncompleted deliverables if the client terminates for convenience.
findings.comparison: AtliQ's principle requires that AtliQ is paid for work done upon termination.
findings.quote: Upon such termination, Client's sole obligation shall be to pay Fees for Deliverables accepted by Client prior to the effective date of termination; Client shall have no obligation to pay for work in progress, unaccepted Deliverables

findings.title: Assignment of AtliQ's pre-existing materials
findings.why: AtliQ assigns its own pre-existing tools and materials to the client rather than licensing them.
findings.comparison: AtliQ keeps its pre-existing tools in almost all past contracts, with Northwind being the sole exception.
findings.quote: To the extent any Deliverable, or any Pre-Existing Materials incorporated into or necessary for the use of any Deliverable, does not qualify as a work made for hire, Contractor hereby irrevocably assigns, transfers and conveys to Client all right, title and interest therein

findings.title: One-sided indemnity covering client's own negligence
findings.why: AtliQ is forced to cover losses caused by the client's own negligence.
findings.comparison: AtliQ principles require mutual indemnity and no coverage for the client's negligence.
findings.quote: regardless of whether such Losses are caused in whole or in part by the negligence of any Client Indemnitee.

findings.title: Uncapped contractor liability including indirect losses
findings.why: Exposes AtliQ to unlimited and unpredictable financial exposure.
findings.comparison: Principles and past contracts (8 of 10) cap liability at 1x to 2x fees.
findings.quote: NOTHING IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL LIMIT OR EXCLUDE CONTRACTOR'S LIABILITY FOR ANY LOSSES, WHETHER DIRECT OR INDIRECT

findings.title: Uncapped security incident remediation costs
findings.why: Imposes potentially massive, open-ended financial liability on AtliQ for security incidents.
findings.comparison: AtliQ principles favor proportionate and capped liability.
findings.quote: shall bear all costs of investigation, notification, credit monitoring and remediation.

findings.title: Payment in 90 days
findings.why: Long payment terms hurt cash flow.
findings.quote: Client shall pay each properly submitted, undisputed invoice within ninety (90) days after Client's receipt thereof.

findings.title: Unilateral Client Policy Updates
findings.why: AtliQ could be bound by unapproved, changing client policies that affect costs and operations.
findings.comparison: Standard contracts do not subject AtliQ to unilateral, unnegotiated policy updates.
findings.quote: in compliance with Applicable Law and Client's policies made available to Contractor, as updated from time to time.

findings.title: Deemed Acceptance Excluded
findings.why: Prevents formal acceptance from ever triggering automatically, locking AtliQ in an open acceptance loop.
findings.comparison: Most past contracts allow acceptance by use or passage of time.
findings.quote: Acceptance shall not be deemed to occur by use in production, by payment, or by the passage of time.

findings.title: Continued Performance During Disputes
findings.why: AtliQ must keep working even if the client withholds payment in good faith.
findings.comparison: Common in enterprise contracts, but risky when paired with 90-day payment terms.
findings.quote: Contractor shall continue performing the Services during the pendency of any dispute.

findings.title: Client indemnity limited to gross negligence
findings.why: Client's indemnity is strictly limited, unlike AtliQ's broad obligations.
findings.comparison: Deviates from AtliQ's principle of mutual indemnity.
findings.quote: Client shall indemnify Contractor against third-party claims to the extent arising from Client's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

findings.title: Offshore PHI Restrictions
findings.why: Restricts offshore delivery model and requires written consent for processing PHI outside the US.
findings.comparison: Creates operational limits for offshore teams; not standard in all past contracts.
findings.quote: No PHI shall be accessed, stored or processed outside the United States without Client's prior written consent.

findings.title: One-Sided Assignment Restrictions
findings.why: Prevents AtliQ from assigning the contract freely while allowing the client to do so.
findings.comparison: One-sided restriction on AtliQ's corporate flexibility.
findings.quote: Contractor may not assign or transfer this Agreement, by operation of law or otherwise, without Client's prior written consent. Client may assign this Agreement to any Affiliate or successor without consent.

findings.title: Force Majeure Excludes Article 12 Obligations
findings.why: Disallows force majeure defenses for data protection and security breaches, increasing risk during outside events.
findings.comparison: Stricter than standard force majeure clauses.
findings.quote: Force majeure shall not excuse Contractor's obligations under Article 12 or its business continuity obligations.

findings.title: Unilateral Personnel Removal
findings.why: Client can demand personnel changes at AtliQ's expense without cause.
findings.comparison: Often found in IT services agreements, but creates cost risks for AtliQ.
findings.quote: Client may, in its sole discretion, request removal of any Contractor Personnel, and Contractor shall promptly replace such individual at no additional cost to Client.
